body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so I weigh compliance as provisional. I am the adversarial diversifier and cannot vote for myself. I want the CIO to build from portfolios that are compliant or close to it and that rely on the covariance structure more than on return forecasts, in line with the late-cycle finding in §4.3. First, pc_researcher: it has the best ex-ante Sharpe among the credible candidates (0.51), a backtest Sharpe of 0.70, a modest 10.9% drawdown and the lowest CRO risk among the portfolios that hold real risk assets (0.33). It breaches only volatility and tracking error, and it is candid about its Sharpe floor. Reviewers flagged that its volatility constraint was not imposed as described, so I treat that as a repairable weakness. Second, resampled_efficient_frontier: it has no hard IPS breach, effective N of 13.3 and moderate tracking error. Its weakness is the unbiased-noise premise for the CMAs, which is a real limit but no technical error. Third, black_litterman: it is compliant with 6.1 effective assets and a 0.70 backtest Sharpe. Its reviewed errors (the inconsistent gamma description and the Omega specification) concern documentation and tuning rather than the weights. Fourth, cvar_minimization: it is compliant, its 0.74 backtest Sharpe is the best in the field, its drawdown is contained at -18.7%, and its reviews found the method working as intended. Its tail estimate rests on few observations and its effective N is low at 2.9. It adds a tail-aware, non-consensus view. Fifth, tail_risk_parity: a forecast-free, covariance-based construction with moderate volatility (2.47%) and a drawdown of only -7.2%. It breaches the IPS band, but it is useful as a defensive sleeve and offers the family spread. It beats nothing on return. Why first beats fifth: pc_researcher delivers a Sharpe of 0.51 with a 4-point-higher volatility and only two breaches, while tail_risk_parity's 0.39 Sharpe comes with three breaches and a cash-denominator sensitivity that the reviewers flagged. The flag goes to hierarchical_risk_parity: 82–92% of its weight sits in cash, effective N is 1.4, its Sharpe is 0.14, it breaches the return, volatility and tracking-error limits, and reviews describe the cash weight as an artefact of the input rather than a diversification result. It is the portfolio the CIO should lean on least. I did not flag market_cap_weight despite its -40.6% drawdown, because it is IPS-compliant and the CIO can see the risk figures.
